about: Known scam scripts, for grounding the judgement step (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5). Written in our own words from the linked public guidance; each card links its sources. The 'name' is what a heads-up says: 'This call sounds like the <name> described by <publisher>'.

cards.name: grandparent scam
cards.description: Someone calls posing as a grandchild or other relative, or as a lawyer or police officer acting for one, with a sudden emergency such as an arrest, a crash or a hospital stay, often while travelling. The voice may sound like the relative's. They need money at once and beg you not to tell the rest of the family.
tells: claims to be a grandchild or relative, or speaks for one
arrest, accident, hospital or trouble abroad
asks you to keep it secret from family
insists it must happen today
a second person takes over as lawyer, officer or bail agent
asks_for: bail, legal fees or medical bills
cash handed to a courier who comes to the door

sources.title: Criminals Pose as Grandchildren in Grandparent Scams
Scammers Use Fake Emergencies To Steal Your Money

cards.name: government impersonation scam
cards.description: A caller claims to be from a government agency, such as the police, the FTC or a benefits office, and says there is a problem with your identity, your benefits or the law. They threaten arrest, fines or losing benefits unless you pay or confirm personal details right away.
tells: claims to be a government agency or officer
threat of arrest, fines or losing benefits
demands immediate action on this call
tells you not to hang up or talk to anyone
asks_for: payment of a fine or fee
Social Security number, bank details or date of birth

sources.title: How To Avoid a Government Impersonation Scam

cards.name: Social Security impersonation scam
cards.description: A caller says they are from the Social Security Administration and that your number has been suspended, used in a crime, or that your benefits will stop. To fix it you must confirm your number or move money, sometimes with a fake badge number or a spoofed caller ID.
tells: says your Social Security number is suspended or involved in a crime
threatens to stop benefits
gives a badge or case number to sound official
caller ID shows a government name
asks_for: your Social Security number
payment to 'protect' your benefits or account

sources.publisher: Social Security Administration Office of the Inspector General
sources.title: Scam Awareness
How to Spot New Social Security Scams

cards.name: IRS tax scam
cards.description: A caller claims to be from the IRS and says you owe back taxes or penalties. They threaten arrest, deportation or losing your licence unless you pay immediately, usually by a method the IRS never uses.
tells: claims to be from the IRS
says you owe back taxes today
threatens arrest or deportation
no letter was ever sent first
asks_for: immediate payment of taxes or penalties

sources.title: Recognize tax scams and fraud

cards.name: jury duty scam
cards.description: A caller says they are a court officer or deputy and that you missed jury duty, so there is a warrant for your arrest. The warrant can be cleared by paying a fine now, or by confirming personal details.
tells: says you missed jury duty
an arrest warrant has been issued
offers to clear it over the phone
claims to be a court officer or sheriff's deputy
asks_for: a fine to cancel the warrant
Social Security number or date of birth

sources.title: Juror Scams

cards.name: Medicare benefits scam
cards.description: A caller claiming to be from Medicare, or working with it, offers a new Medicare card, free medical equipment, a free test or extra benefits, and needs your Medicare number to 'verify' you or process it.
tells: claims to be from Medicare
offers a new card, free equipment, braces or genetic tests
asks you to confirm your Medicare number
benefits will be lost if you do not act
asks_for: your Medicare number
Social Security number or bank details

sources.title: How Beneficiaries Can Prevent Medicare Fraud
Reporting Medicare fraud & abuse

cards.name: health insurance scam
cards.description: A caller sells a health plan that sounds unusually cheap or complete, often claiming to be from a government marketplace. It turns out to be a limited discount plan or nothing at all, and they want payment or card details on the call.
tells: cold call selling a health plan
price far below normal
claims government or marketplace backing
you must enrol today
asks_for: card or bank details to enrol
Social Security or Medicare number

sources.title: How Scammers Target People Looking for Health Insurance

cards.name: tech support scam
cards.description: A caller, or a pop-up message with a number to call, claims to be from Microsoft, Apple or your internet provider and says your computer has a virus or has been hacked. They want to take control of the computer and charge you to fix a problem that does not exist.
tells: claims to be Microsoft, Apple or your internet provider
says your computer has a virus or was hacked
asks you to install a program or give remote access
a pop-up told you to call a number
asks_for: remote access to your computer
payment for repairs or a support plan

sources.title: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams

cards.name: phantom hacker scam
cards.description: A scam in stages. A fake tech support caller says your computer or bank account has been hacked. Then a fake bank fraud officer says your savings are at risk, and sometimes a fake government official backs them up. You are told to move your money into a 'safe' account for protection, and told to keep it secret.
tells: one caller hands you on to a second or third
says your bank or computer has been hacked
tells you to move money to protect it
says not to tell the bank staff or family why
asks_for: transfer of savings to a 'safe' or 'government' account
cash or gold collected by a courier
remote access to your computer

sources.title: "Phantom Hacker" Scams Target Senior Citizens

cards.name: bank impostor scam
cards.description: A caller says they are from your bank's fraud department and have spotted suspicious activity. To 'secure' the account they ask for a code sent to your phone, your card number or PIN, or ask you to move money to a new account.
tells: claims to be your bank's fraud team
reports suspicious charges
asks you to read back a code sent by text
asks for your PIN, card number or login
asks_for: a one-time code
card number, PIN or online banking login
moving money to a new account

sources.title: "Phantom Hacker" Scams Target Senior Citizens
Phone Scams

cards.name: utility shutoff scam
cards.description: A caller claiming to be from the electric, gas or water company says your bill is overdue and your service will be cut off within the hour unless you pay now.
tells: claims to be the utility company
service cut off today, often within an hour
demands payment on this call
asks_for: immediate payment of an overdue bill

sources.title: How To Protect Yourself From Utility Scams

cards.name: prize or lottery scam
cards.description: A caller says you have won a lottery, sweepstakes or prize, sometimes one you never entered. To collect it you must first pay taxes, fees or shipping, or give your bank details for the deposit.
tells: says you won a prize or lottery
you must pay to collect
a contest you do not remember entering
asks_for: fees, taxes or shipping in advance
bank details for the 'deposit'

sources.title: Fake Prize, Sweepstakes, and Lottery Scams

cards.name: gift card payment scam
cards.description: Whatever the story, the caller wants payment in gift cards: you are told to buy them at a store and read out the numbers on the back. No real business or agency takes payment this way.
tells: asks you to buy gift cards
asks for the numbers on the back of the card
stays on the line while you shop
asks_for: gift card numbers and PINs

sources.title: Avoiding and Reporting Gift Card Scams

cards.name: romance scam
cards.description: Someone met online or by message builds a close, affectionate relationship over weeks, but can never meet in person: they say they work abroad, on an oil rig or a ship, in the military, or as a doctor overseas. Then they need money: for a ticket to visit, a medical bill, customs or release fees, or an investment they want to share.
tells: a sweetheart known only online or by phone
works abroad, on an oil rig, at sea or in the military
always a reason they cannot meet yet
customs, release or travel fees stand in the way of visiting
promises to pay you back
asks_for: money for a ticket, medical bills, customs or release fees
money for an investment

sources.title: What To Know About Romance Scams
How to Protect Yourself Against Online Romance Scams

cards.name: investment or cryptocurrency scam
cards.description: A caller or new contact offers a can't-lose investment, often in cryptocurrency, gold or a 'special' fund, with guaranteed high returns. Early 'profits' appear on a website, but money put in cannot be taken out.
tells: guaranteed or very high returns
pressure to invest quickly
cryptocurrency, gold or an exclusive opportunity
asks you to send money to a new platform or wallet
asks_for: money to invest
transfer to a crypto wallet or ATM

sources.title: What To Know About Cryptocurrency and Scams
How to Spot and Protect Yourself From Investment Fraud

cards.name: refund or recovery scam
cards.description: Someone contacts a person who has already lost money to a scam, offering to recover it for a fee, sometimes posing as a lawyer or a government agency. Or a caller says you are owed a refund and 'accidentally' sends too much, asking for the difference back.
tells: offers to recover money you lost
claims to be a lawyer or agency helping victims
says you were overpaid a refund
wants a fee first
asks_for: an upfront recovery fee
repayment of an 'overpaid' refund

sources.title: Refund and Recovery Scams

cards.name: charity scam
cards.description: A caller asks for a donation for a cause that sounds worthy, often after a disaster or for veterans, police or firefighters. They are vague about the charity, push for money right now, and want cash, gift cards or a wire.
tells: asks for a donation now
vague about the charity's name or work
thanks you for a donation you never made
wants cash, gift cards or a wire
asks_for: a donation today

sources.title: Before Giving to a Charity
How to Tell If a Charity Is a Fraud

cards.name: home repair scam
cards.description: A contractor turns up uninvited or calls, often after a storm, saying your roof, driveway or chimney needs urgent work. They offer a special price if you agree today and want a large deposit up front, then do poor work or none.
tells: unsolicited offer of repairs
leftover materials or a special price today
large deposit or full payment up front
no written contract
asks_for: a cash deposit before work starts

sources.title: Here's How to Hire a Reliable Contractor

cards.name: fake debt collector scam
cards.description: A caller says you owe a debt, sometimes one you do not recognise, and threatens arrest, a lawsuit or wage garnishment unless you pay immediately. They will not send details in writing.
tells: a debt you do not recognise
threatens arrest or lawsuit
refuses to send written details
demands payment on this call
asks_for: immediate payment of the debt
bank account details

sources.title: Debt Collection FAQs

cards.name: robocall sales scam
cards.description: A recorded message or pushy caller offers to lower your credit card interest rate, extend your car's warranty, or sell a medical alert device or other service, and asks you to press a key and give card or personal details.
tells: a recorded message
offers to lower your interest rate or extend a car warranty
press a number to speak to someone
pressure to sign up now
asks_for: card number or bank details
an upfront fee

sources.title: Phone Scams

cards.name: fake check scam
cards.description: Someone sends you a check, for a prize, a sale or a job, for more than they owe, and asks you to deposit it and send the difference back. The check later bounces and the money you sent is gone.
tells: a check for more than expected
asks you to send part of it back
urgency to send the money before the check clears
asks_for: return of the 'extra' money

sources.title: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Fake Check Scams

cards.name: payment app scam
cards.description: Someone says they sent you money by mistake on a payment app like Zelle, Venmo or Cash App and asks you to send it back, or a caller claiming to be from the app says your account needs 'verifying' with a payment.
tells: says they paid you by mistake
asks you to send money back through the app
claims to be app support
a payment you did not expect
asks_for: money sent back through the app
your app login or a code

sources.title: Mobile Payment Apps: How To Avoid a Scam When You Use One
